events.excerpt: Parallel parking would be a whole lot easier if cars could slide sideways into a parking space. Of course, normal wheels don't work that way. But that didn't stop robotics enthusiast James Bruton from building a vehicle that can do exactly that. His latest creation is a rideable, self-driving electric car that can move in any direction without turning. The secret is an unusual set of wheels inspired by research from Osaka University. Instead of using conventional tires or standard omnidirectional wheels, Bruton built four large ball-wheels, each consisting of two hemispheres mounted on a T-shaped axle. The hemispheres are driven together in one direction but can roll freely in the perpendicular direction. With all four wheels mounted at 45-degree angles around the chassis, the vehicle can move forward, backward, sideways, diagonally, or rotate on the spot. To make the wheels, Bruton used a CNC machine to cut plywood into interlocking pieces, assembling 14 vertical ribs and several horizontal layers to form each hemisphere. He then added rubberized edging for traction and 3D-printed domes to complete the rounded shape. Small skateboard wheels hidden inside the tips allow the hemispheres to roll smoothly even when the vehicle's weight rests on their ends. The chassis and wheel axle
events.headline: James Bruton Reinvents the Wheel, Literally

events.excerpt: Anthropic has introduced three new types of artifacts that show the company tiptoeing into the office productivity market long dominated by Microsoft and Google. On Tuesday, the Claudefather announced Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards, and Claude Data, and promised the imminent arrival of Claude Meetings. These artifact types join existing ones – Docs, Slides, Design, and Motion – to form a nascent Claude-dependent productivity suite. Anthropic initially used the term artifacts to refer to shareable AI-based interactive tools, like dynamic charts. But the scope of the term has been stretched to cover specific artifact types, which refer to what traditionalists might take to mean files associated with specific hosted applications. "An artifact is anything Claude makes for you that you'd put in front of someone: a design, a deck, a document, a dashboard, or a small interactive tool," the company explains. The key thing that distinguishes an artifact from a file is that users are meant to interact with artifacts through Claude, rather than storing and transferring them independently. Think of it more as a container or managed object that opens in Claude (via a sharing URL), because artifacts in fact consist of various content types – .txt, .md, .html, .jsx, .svg, .pptx, .docx, .zip,
events.headline: Anthropic tiptoes into MS Office territory

events.excerpt: Server consolidation has led Cisco to boost the speed of top-of-rack switches to 100G. The networking giant last week announced the catchily named N9348C8D-H2, a 1U device packing 48 100G SFP-DD ports and eight 400G QSFP-DD uplinks. At the Cisco Live event in Melbourne, Australia, this week, Cisco’s senior veep for datacenter and internet infrastructure, Kevin Wollenweber, said one reason the company created the device is that modern servers often feature a pair of fast network interface cards. The twin cards are needed because sixth-gen server processors from Intel and AMD offer dozens, or even hundreds, of physical processor cores and therefore generate a lot of traffic. The density of computing power those processors provide has led chipmakers and server manufacturers to suggest replacing handfuls of machines running older, power-guzzling Xeons and Epycs with boxes running more efficient sixth-gen chips. The Register hears it’s not uncommon to achieve 6:1 server consolidation ratios when moving from third- or fourth-generation Xeons or Epycs to current models. Users who make that move can pack many more server cores into the same rack. Power bills go down, but the quantity of data leaving a rack goes up. Wollenweber said Cisco realized it had “tons” of switches that offer 25G
events.headline: Ye olde server consolidation has made Cisco push top-of-rack switching to 100G

events.excerpt: Advocates for cloud-native software have long argued that their approach to development makes applications portable across different Kubernetes environments. But VMware argues that’s not happening across hybrid clouds, and has taken the lead in an effort to improve matters. That effort, the new Workload Conformance Working Group in the Kubernetes community, aims to establish a shared standard for how workloads run on Kubernetes. The group’s web page points out, “Certified Kubernetes tests the cluster, and Kubernetes AI Conformance tests whether a cluster can run AI and ML workloads. Nothing comparable exists for the workloads themselves, so cluster operators still check each application by hand before routine maintenance or a Kubernetes upgrade. Every cluster operator ends up repeating the same assessment, and application maintainers get the same questions from each environment they support,” the group asserts. The proposed solution? “A common specification with repeatable tests would give both groups the same baseline to start from.” Prashanth Shenoy, VP of product marketing in Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) division, told The Register that standard is needed in part because applications packaged to run in public clouds don’t always run well in hybrid clouds. events.excerpt: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month’s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws — including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook — and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe , Apple , Google and Mozilla . Image: Shutterstock.com. Diorama by @zepp1969. November’s patch release from Redmond tackles 1,093 vulnerabilities, fixing 63 “critical” flaws that can be exploited to seize control over a Windows system with little or no help from users. Nearly half of those critical bugs are remote code execution vulnerabilities. Overall, 535 of the flaws addressed this month allow an attacker to elevate their privileges on a vulnerable device. This latest round of updates means Microsoft has shipped more than 5,100 security patches so far this year, a staggering number considering that a year ago Microsoft was averaging around 100 patches per month. Microsoft credits advances in artificial intelligence for helping to find (and fix) such a large volume of security bugs in recent months. Last month, Microsoft pushed more than 1,400 fixes. According to Redmond, just one of the flaws is already seeing active exploit
events.headline: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities

events.excerpt: Goldman Sachs, Citi and the other Project Faro members have committed funding to a jointly owned dollar stablecoin issuer. The money covers years of operating costs and has nothing to do with token reserves. The venture still has no CEO, no final name and no disclosed blockchain. A rival group of European banks already holds a license for its own euro stablecoin. A group of 21 banks and asset managers, including Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Banco Santander and Deutsche Bank, has committed roughly $270 million to the company that will issue its planned U.S. dollar stablecoin, according to people familiar with the discussions. The commitments, reported on November 10, are meant to fund about five years of operations for the venture, known internally as Project Faro, which targets a launch in the first half of 2027 and would compete with Tether and Circle for institutional dollar payments. The $270 million pays for the issuer itself, meaning staff, technology, compliance and licensing, while the reserves backing each token will come later from the clients who buy them. The reporting does not show how much each institution contributed or whether all 21 members are paying in. A spokesperson for the project declined to comment, Goldman Sachs and Citi referred questions to the consortium,
events.headline: Goldman, Citi Bet $270M on Project Faro to Rival Tether

events.excerpt: Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears. The threat is especially serious for AI agents with tool or terminal access. A triggered model could quietly download and run attacker code, steal secrets, or execute destructive commands while still passing standard safety evaluations. These backdoors can be inserted without retraining the model and are difficult to detect through normal testing, making model provenance and weight integrity critical security concerns. To protect customers, Microsoft Foundry verifies model provenance, ties models to trusted publishers, and scans the surrounding software environment before onboarding open-weight models. Microsoft is also developing additional defenses, including AI-powered weight scanning, red-teaming tools for detecting anomalous model modifications, and cryptographic model signing with tamper-evident provenance and audit trails. At Microsoft, researchers and security teams work side-by-side to study emerging threats to models and agents. events.excerpt: Now that LLMs can help analyze commercial software binaries and recreate their functionality, one software developer and student has created a project designed to make this process more difficult. Timo Zhang's project is called Blind LLM Agents (BLA), and as its name suggests, it attempts to interfere with efforts by AI agents to scrutinize app code. "Coding agents can reverse-engineer shipped packages, CLIs, and WASM in minutes," Zhang told The Register in an email. "Classic obfuscation was built for humans and static tools, not LLMs that reason about meaning. Blind LLM Agents is a protection layer for that threat model." Such agents can also help developers build alternatives to existing commercial software. Last month, Artcraft , a two-person development shop, released seven open-source apps that aim to be replacements for Adobe's commercial apps Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro. Artcraft claims these apps are "clean-room reimplementations" written from scratch in Rust using Anthropic Opus 5.5. events.excerpt: This proposal specifies the JSON document that tokenURI returns in ERC-721 and ERC-6909 and that uri returns in ERC-1155 . Most deployed tokens already use this format, but only part of it was ever specified. ERC-721 and ERC-1155 define name , description and image . Everything else wallets and marketplaces show ( animation_url , attributes and its display_type values, external_url , background_color ) comes from a page OpenSea published in 2018. Clients fill the gaps differently, so the same token renders differently from one app to the next. Draft: erc-8495.md ( ethereum/ERCs#2163 ) The draft covers: Every field and its type, every display_type value in use, and what clients do with values that don’t match, such as booleans, quoted numbers and dates in milliseconds. The URI schemes clients must resolve ( https , ipfs , ar , data ), the ones they may resolve ( ipns , and web3 from ERC-4804 ), and the ones they must never resolve. Fetching rules: ipfs:// URIs instead of gateway URLs, sandboxing HTML in animation_url , and keeping server-side fetches away from private addresses. events.excerpt: We recommend that all atlantic-2 validators and node operators update to v6.8.0-rc3 . The update is required for RPC nodes. There is no governance proposal and no coordinated chain halt. v6.8.0-rc3 is a release candidate on top of v6.8.0-rc2 . It makes wide eth_getLogs queries cheaper for RPC nodes and stops them early when the client cancels ( #4744 , #4790 , #4791 , #4799 , #4802 ). It also includes the v6.7.4 trace fix, so debug_trace* loads a past block's full validator set ( #4811 ). Wide log queries (over 100 blocks) share a node-wide limit of 30 queries per second. You can now change it with large_log_query_rps under [evm] in app.toml . Set it to 0 to turn the limit off. If the key is missing, the limit stays at 30 ( #4800 ). How to Update Build v6.8.0-rc3 with git fetch --tags && git checkout v6.8.0-rc3 && make install . Stop the node. Replace the seid binary with v6.8.0-rc3 . If you use Cosmovisor, replace the binary in upgrades/v6.8/bin/ . Start the node. Make sure that seid version shows v6.8.0-rc3 and that the node syncs new blocks.
